terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; with ad, adversus or the dative
evidence: Sen. Ep. 6.5: breve et efficāx per exempla
terms.comment: Mostly post-Augustan; not in Cicero or Caesar, though Caelius uses it in a letter to Cicero (Fam. 8.10.3) (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: to have force, to work, to be effective
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.17.1: valēbunt autem semper arma (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First “be strong, be well”; transferred, “have power, prevail, avail”.

terms.gloss: to achieve something; nihil prōficere, to have no effect
evidence: Caes. B.G. 7.20: sī nihil in oppugnātiōne oppidī prōfēcisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also “make progress”, and of things “be of use”.

phrases.latin: longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla
phrases.english: the road through rules is long; through examples it is short and effective
good at washing away the bitterness of cares

phrases.latin: Hoc medicāmentum adversus tussim efficāx est.
phrases.english: This medicine is effective against a cough.

sources: Lewis & Short: efficax · Lewis & Short: valeo · Lewis & Short: proficio
